prompt.context: Portkey Inc. is a British company that has developed a new technology, Apparate, that can transport a person in a matter of seconds. The founder, Albus Severus Potter, invented the technology when he needed a fast way to travel from McMuggle to the Hogwarts School of Management. Apparate is the first technology of its kind, patented, and does not have any direct competitors. Up-front fixed costs are estimated to be 2.3BN GBP.
prompt.question: Albus has tasked us with figuring out whether to launch Apparate, and if launched – how to price this new service.

clarifying_info.q: In which markets has Apparate received regulatory approval?
clarifying_info.a: The UK is the only country that has given regulatory approval.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any consumer research on willingness to use Apparate?
clarifying_info.a: From an initial consumer survey, 60% of travelers indicated they are open to this new mode of travel.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any known safety issues?
clarifying_info.a: From initial testing, out of 200,000 people, one person experienced half-a-body delay – an often fatal condition.

clarifying_info.q: Does the risk profile vary by trip?
clarifying_info.a: The trip is instant, but the technology's risks increase as trip distance increases.

exhibits.title: UK Travel Market Data
exhibits.shows: A table of UK travel market statistics relevant to sizing a 400-mile trip market (e.g. London to Edinburgh).

framework: Enter market? — assess whether Portkey Inc. should launch Apparate
Market attractiveness — market size, growth and trends, consumer interest
Pricing — value-based vs. cost-based pricing strategy
Other considerations — risks, regulations, competitive dynamics, company objectives, product development

questions.prompt: Calculate the potential size of the market for a 400-mile trip (e.g. London to Edinburgh), focusing on the UK market for 400-mile airplane trips.
questions.guidance: Candidate should break the market into Price × Quantity and recognise two customer segments: business and leisure travellers. Candidate should request or brainstorm the inputs needed (route, ticket price, number of travellers, trip frequency) before receiving Exhibit A. Candidate should note this is a large and growing market (2% YoY) and may mention that business tickets tend to be pricier than leisure. A logical next step is breakeven: at £100/trip, 23MM trips needed (8% of 304MM total trips).

math.setup: Market size = Price × Quantity. Quantity split by segment: Business travellers = 60M × 0.66 × 0.80 × 9 trips; Leisure travellers = 60M × 0.66 × 0.20 × 2 trips. Price = £100/trip.
steps: Breakeven trips at £100/trip = £2.3BN / £100 = 23MM trips = ~8% market share
math.answer: £30.4BN total market (304MM trips); breakeven requires ~23MM trips (~8% share) at £100/trip.

questions.prompt: As a next step, assess pricing strategies. What price would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a second framework covering pricing approaches. Key insight: Apparate should be value-based priced because (1) low breakeven threshold, (2) no direct competition, and (3) high price of substitutes. Candidate should not be anchored to the £100 exhibit price. Strong answers may also mention: target-return pricing (set price to break even in 1 year), psychological pricing (high price as quality signal), how to value time saved (work hours, opportunity cost), and possible introductory discounts to overcome consumer hesitancy with a new product.

recommendation: Portkey Inc. should move forward with launching Apparate
The UK market for short-haul trips is £30.4BN and growing at 2% a year
There are no direct competitors and the technology is patented
A value-based pricing strategy positions the company for future growth while funding R&D
risks: Safety risk: product malfunctioning (1 in 200,000 experienced half-a-body delay, often fatal)
Lack of consumer adoption of a genuinely new-to-world product
Changes in regulatory environment or restrictions on commercialising the technology in other geographies
Competitive entry eroding the basis for value-based pricing
next_steps: Complete a rigorous, publicly available safety study to build consumer confidence
Conduct market research to better understand consumer interest, needs, and value creation levers
Choose a pilot market and/or segment (e.g. business travellers) and conduct a controlled test launch
